A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ANTS, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable. v1 includes supplementary sections A and B; v3 ends after the references despite citing supplementary results. This limits comparison of supplement-only experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet and OpenOOD experiments, component ablations, robustness analyses and supplementary case studies.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results and ablations, including newly presented initial-detector and sentence-length analyses.

M1.justification: The ENS/VSNL framework and adaptive scoring remain. However, v3 changes VSNL class-frequency estimation and generation inputs from mined negative images to historical test images (Eqs. 9–12), and Figure 4 adds an under-eight-word generation instruction. Historical-stream processing already appeared in v1 Algorithm 1, so the greater emphasis on caching is not itself a new method.

E1.justification: The documented ImageNet/OpenOOD coverage is retained. The four ID datasets in v3 Table 3 already appeared in v1 Table 11. However, v3 defers small-scale near-OOD and domain/adversarial robustness results to unavailable supplementary material. Retention of v1's ImageNet-S/A/R/V2 evaluations, and whether the adversarial claim represents a distinct new scenario, cannot be established.

E2.justification: v3 adds SynOOD to Tables 1 and 2 and removes TagOOD and CLIPScope rows from Table 1. Its four-ID-dataset summary retains NegLabel but omits the MCM and EOE comparisons reported in v1 Table 11. CoVer remains; only its duplicate training-required row disappears. These are changes within the retained comparison framework.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported negative-label count from 5,000 to 10,000, without establishing which experiments were rerun. New analyses vary initialization detectors and sentence length; the displayed selection-ratio sweep also changes. The main backbone, evaluation metrics, temperature and mining defaults remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 7 adds investigations of dependence on the initial detector and generated-sentence length. Figure 6b replaces the near/far threshold comparison with Texture/SUN curves. Temporal-shift analysis is retained from v1 Figure 8, not newly introduced. v1's noise-rate plot, alternative-weighting comparison and case studies are absent from the supplied v3; their retention elsewhere cannot be verified.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. Dataset averages and classification-confidence examples do not constitute uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes ANTS's average AUROC/FPR95 from 97.40/13.31 to 97.75/11.20. These are revised results under a changed reported label budget, not an established same-setting gain. SynOOD results and new sensitivity curves are added. v3 Table 3 also changes NegLabel's CUB AUROC from v1 Table 11's 99.96 to 99.93. ANTS's aggregate OpenOOD, component-ablation and throughput results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The definition of class frequency F(yi) changes from a proportion over mined negatives in v1 Eq. 11 to a proportion over historical test images in v3 Eq. 10. This changes the mathematical population, rather than merely renumbering the equation. The remaining scoring mathematics is substantially retained, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central training-free, zero-shot, adaptive near/far-OOD claims remain. The headline FPR95 reduction changes from 4.2% to 3.1%, consistent with comparison against different strongest listed baselines: CSP in v1 and SynOOD in v3. The contribution list additionally states that auxiliary outlier images are unnecessary.

C2.justification: Section 6 substantially narrows the limitation account: v1 identifies initial-detector dependence, the need for many negative images and MLLM overhead; v3 states only GPU-memory demand, calling it a minor limitation. v3 also adds an interpretation of sentence length as a tradeoff between expressiveness and hallucinated or nondiscriminative words, and discusses robustness with weaker initialization detectors.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly identifies LLaVA-1.5-7B as the default MLLM, documents the revised 10,000-label setting and explains historical-image caching more clearly. v1 already named LLaVA-7B in its model comparison but did not explicitly specify this default. The repository address, RTX 3090 hardware disclosure and throughput table are retained.

R1.justification: v3 removes the dedicated MLLM related-work discussion, its industrial-anomaly comparisons and explicit first-use positioning for large-scale OOD detection. The reconstruction-based category also disappears. It adds citations to Dai et al.'s multimodal OOD work and SynOOD. The updated publication entry for knowledge-regularized negative feature tuning represents the same work, not a new citation.

P1.justification: The title and author-name ordering change, historical-test terminology is clarified, and several discussion paragraphs and the conclusion are rewritten or condensed. Related work loses a subsection, while selected supplementary findings enter the main text. The main section sequence and much of the methodological prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is substantially redrawn to separate historical-data caching from current-image scoring. Figure 6 changes panels and axes; Figure 7 becomes an eight-panel display incorporating the earlier temporal-shift figure. v1 Table 11 is condensed into v3 Table 3, and several supplementary tables and case-study figures are not included. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies online operation, adds a strong comparator and investigates detector dependence and sentence length. However, important robustness evidence is deferred to supplementary material absent from the supplied PDF, while substantive limitations are removed from Section 6. These gaps prevent a reliable net-quality judgment. The lower reported ImageNet FPR95 does not resolve the tradeoff because the reported label budget also changes.
